problem.title: S3 503 Slow Down Throttling on Concentrated Prefix Naming Patterns
problem.prompt: Batch processing pipeline downloading 20,000 files/sec from AWS S3 using prefix 's3://my-bucket/logs/2026-11-02/'.
requirements: Operational Invariant: "Partition object storage keys across multiple distinct prefixes to scale beyond single-prefix IOPS boundaries."
Production Hardening: Distribute workloads across multiple prefixes by prepending a hash prefix or customer ID ('s3://my-bucket/partition-a8f/logs/...') or use multi-part parallel range requests.

stages.learnerPrompt: What catastrophic failure physics occur when capacity limits or downstream dependencies degrade under peak load?

referenceMaterial.summary: Failure physics analysis: 100k QPS → TTL Expiration → Cache Miss Herd → Origin Slam → 💥 DB Meltdown.
failureModes: Cascading Failure: Amazon S3 automatically scales partitions based on object key prefixes, offering 3,500 PUT and 5,500 GET requests per second per prefix. Concentrating 20,000 requests on a single prefix triggers HTTP 503 Slow Down throttles.
Breakdown Chain: 100k QPS → TTL Expiration → Cache Miss Herd → Origin Slam → 💥 DB Meltdown
Shedding Failure: Without fast rejection at the boundary, queued dead work triggers multi-second GC pauses, CPU thrashing, and cascading 504 Gateway Timeouts.

stages.learnerPrompt: How does the system enforce physical resource boundaries under sudden downstream latency brownouts?

referenceMaterial.summary: Senior Staff SRE Interview challenge and architectural invariant verification.
tradeOffs: Architectural Invariant: "Partition object storage keys across multiple distinct prefixes to scale beyond single-prefix IOPS boundaries."
Physical Resource Boundary: Dynamic admission control ensures worker threads never buffer dead requests during downstream brownouts.
approachSteps: 1. Track real-time latency gradients and inflight concurrency.
2. Reject excess traffic at the ingress boundary within <0.1ms.
3. Monitor P99 latency and verify autonomous recovery when downstream pressure subsides.
